brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 124524 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 74% over 10s (8/31 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $4,748/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 124524) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $4,748/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: The root blocker (pid 124524) has been idle for only 4.0s, well within the business tolerance of 60s of degraded checkout (BIZ-1). The transaction is idle-in-transaction with last statement SELECT 1, suggesting minimal active work. Terminating risks aborting an adhoc_reporting job with no registry entry (BIZ-2) and unknown cost (BIZ-4). Waiting allows natural lock release without blast radius. The trade-off analysis (BIZ-4) confirms interrupting has unknown cost due to missing registry entry, making wait the safer default. Evidence DB-1 confirms 12 sessions waiting but blocker only 4.0s old; BIZ-1 confirms checkout can tolerate up to 60s of degradation; BIZ-3 confirms no active change-calendar window blocks graceful termination. No new evidence argues for immediate termination.

audit.report: The checkout flow degraded after an unknown workload acquired a lock held by session pid 124524 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting). Over 15 seconds, success dropped to 53% (32/60) with 28 timeouts, putting ~$4,748/min of revenue at risk. The root blocker has been idle for only 4.0s and is well within the 60s business tolerance window, with its last statement being a simple SELECT 1. The negotiation escalated because the Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review, leaving the database in a degraded state beyond the verification window.
audit.root_cause: An unknown workload acquired a lock on session pid 124524, blocking checkout sessions and causing a 47% success rate degradation.
lessons: Add adhoc_reporting to the workload registry immediately so cost of interruption and ownership can be evaluated automatically.
Verify the change calendar covers adhoc_reporting before assuming no active window exists; a missed window could block safe termination.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly identified the blocker was within the 60s tolerance and favored waiting, but the Continuity Guardian failed grounding twice, preventing a joint decision and forcing escalation despite clear evidence.
follow_ups: Populate biz.workload_registry for adhoc_reporting with owner and cost metadata.
Check biz.change_calendar for any window covering adhoc_reporting and document the result.
Escalate to the on-call team to resume the negotiation once grounding evidence is provided.

events.title: 3 candidate actions enumerated from observed evidence

candidates.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 124524) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
Hand the decision to the owning team with a decision brief.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 124524) has been idle for only 4.0s. Waiting allows the transaction to complete naturally without terminating a session that may be performing legitimate work. The business tolerance is 60s of degraded checkout, and the blocker is well within that window. Terminating prematurely risks aborting a batch job or report that the owning team may not want killed. New evidence from workload registry and change calendar is needed before committing to terminate.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker finishes within the next few seconds, the 12 waiting checkout sessions will acquire their locks and checkout success rates should recover. If the blocker does not finish, checkout continues to timeout at the current rate (53% success).
proposal.risk_assessment: Continuing to wait risks further checkout timeouts and revenue at risk, but terminating the blocker risks aborting a legitimate batch/ad-hoc job and potentially causing more disruption than the current timeout rate.
